mechanics.name: Blast Mine
mechanics.currentEffect: After you repair Generators for a total of 40%, install a trap on a Generator with the Active Ability button. If the Killer begins damaging it, the trap triggers halfway through the action, stuns the Killer for 4 seconds and blinds players within 12.5 metres. All Survivors see its yellow Aura. The trap expires after 100/110/120 seconds if unused.
activation: Install the trap on a Generator.
Ends/deactivates when: Trap is consumed when triggered or expires after its tier duration.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.2.0): Changed the activation requirement to 40% total Generator repair progress.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: After enough Generator repair, you can booby-trap a Generator to stun the Killer who damages it.
mechanics.oncePerTrialOrOtherLimits: One trap per activation; another requires reactivation.
specialInteractions: Triggers halfway through the Killer's Generator damage action.
Blinds players within 12.5 metres; all Survivors see its yellow Aura.

editorial.summary: After 40% generator repair, trap a Generator for up to 120 seconds; if the Killer kicks it, they are stunned for 4 seconds and nearby players are blinded.
useCases: Punish a Killer who repeatedly returns to kick a contested generator.
Use the yellow Generator Aura to communicate an important objective to teammates.
Buy four seconds of Killer downtime during a regression attempt.
counters: The Killer must actually damage the trapped generator.
The blind can affect nearby Survivors too.
pros: Four-second Killer stun is meaningful time.
Easy to charge through normal repair.
Trap also marks the generator for the team.
cons: Does not stop the initial decision to pressure the generator.
Can become mostly entertainment value if the stunned Killer was not losing meaningful tempo.
analysis: Blast Mine ranks this position because a four-second stun is real Killer downtime attached to normal generator participation. Forty percent total repair is a reasonable charge condition, so many Trials offer multiple opportunities to arm it.

The yellow Aura also gives the perk a communication layer. Teammates can identify the trapped generator and infer that it is strategically important, which matters more in Solo Q than the text first suggests.
The weakness is agency. The Killer can ignore the generator, let the mine expire, or arrive only after the situation no longer matters. Unlike a chase stun, the Survivor cannot force the trigger.
That puts Blast Mine in a useful but conditional band. It is easy, useful, and occasionally disruptive, but too dependent on Killer behavior to outrank more reliable information and support tools.
editorial.verdict: A satisfying and legitimately useful regression punish. Blast Mine buys real time when it triggers, but the Killer decides whether the trigger ever happens.
